comments.author: dhosek
comments.textRawHtml:
On the gadget front, I really love the paperlike screen protector for the iPad. This combined with the Apple Pencil made a huge difference in the usability of my iPad for writing/drawing. I still prefer to write on paper, but it’s really great for things like my writing group where we generally meet over zoom & I can give the author a marked up manuscript (with multicolor notes).

I’m also opposed to getting too precious about writing tools. So many people have drawers full of fancy notebooks with something on the first few pages and the rest empty. Get something and use it. Don’t matter if it’s a dollar-store spiral notebook or a fancy Leuchturm 1917 notebook, just as long as you use it. Same with the writing utensil. Pencil? Ballpoint pen? Whatever. I find these days I prefer to write using a cheap mechanical pencil (the kind they sell in bags of 20 at the supermarket), but I’ll use whatever.

I used to be really precious about these things. I only used college-ruled 9½×6 150-page spiral bound notebooks and wrote in 0.4mm fine-point felt tip pen. Did all my first drafts by hand. It ended up being an excuse to not finish stuff. I do most of my first drafts typing now, because it lets me get s⸻ done (although I still take notes by hand because that helps me remember what I took notes on better).

I don’t buy the cursive thing, mostly because I write slower in cursive than in print (although I have a handful of ligatures and abbreviations I use to speed up some things).

children.author: ksenzee
children.textRawHtml: The cursive thing is almost certainly because he's using fountain pens. Pencils and ballpoint pens lend themselves to printing more easily, because they require pressure to write, and when you let the pressure up between letters, the line stops. The first time I picked up a fountain pen and tried printing with it, I found all my letters were connecting whether I meant them to or not, and I suddenly understood why cursive exists. Everyone who's learned cursive in the ballpoint pen era has been unwittingly taught a performance optimization for a tool they're not using.
children.textZhHtml: 草书几乎可以肯定是因为他使用钢笔。铅笔和圆珠笔更容易打印，因为它们需要压力才能书写，当你在字母之间加大压力时，线条就会停止。当我第一次拿起钢笔尝试用它打印时，我发现我所有的字母都在连接，无论我是否有意，我突然明白了为什么存在草书。每个在圆珠笔时代学过草书的人都在不知不觉中学会了对他们不使用的工具进行性能优化。

children.author: nyrikki
children.textRawHtml:
From the OP:

> "I learned cursive as a child. Then I went for many years without using it much, and forgot some of it."

While fountain pens may be nicer for cursive, they were very late in the games only coming into the scene in the late 1800s, long after fashion had been set.

In the US we were taught either the Zaner-Bloser or the D'Nealian alphabet, and while most of the claims of cursive over manuscript are typically overblown and fall under scrutiny, with common use it may not be faster, but is easer for (the small sample of friends I have asked) to write while not looking at the paper. Not faster, but easier to write in strait lines without looking (in my experience).

Manuscript (now called printing) wasn't common when Zaner-Bloser printed the book "The arm movement method of rapid writing"[0] IIRC.

But for business writing (which both Zaner-Bloser and D'Nealian were targeting) it is not so much the fact that you aren't lifting the point, but that you are using your whole arm.

The scientific claims of Zaner-Bloser are almost certainly suspect, but before word-processors, taking notes while not watching your writing was a critical skill, or was in my experience.

That is a very different world that the scribes of old, or even Roman cursive, which would have only had quills, and which did not really connect letters.

If you look into secretary hand, italic hand, and court hand, a lot of it had to to with style and preferences, with the US Declaration of Independence being in Secretary Hand, which had been in fashion for official docs for centuries at that point. Shakespeare also wrote his plays Secretary Hand, while ladies of the era would have used 'Italian style' italics.

So unfortunately it seems there are many back explanations, the real history is clear as mud in the absence of direct evidence, or more correctly, claims like in Zaner-Bloser.

[0] https://archive.org/details/armmovementmetho00zane/page/n3/m...
children.textZhHtml:
来自OP：

> “我小时候学过草书。后来我很多年都没有怎么用它，并且忘记了一些。”

虽然钢笔可能更适合草写，但它们在游戏中出现的时间很晚，直到 1800 年代末才出现，那时时尚已经定型很久了。

在美国，我们要么被教 Zaner-Bloser，要么被教 D'Nealian 字母表，虽然大多数关于草书优于手稿的说法通常都被夸大了，并且受到审查，但在普遍使用的情况下，它可能不会更快，但更容易（我问过的一小部分朋友）在不看论文的情况下写作。 不是更快，而是更容易在不看的情况下用直线书写（根据我的经验）。

当 Zaner-Bloser 印刷《快速书写的手臂运动方法》一书[0] IIRC 时，手稿（现在称为印刷）并不常见。

但对于商业写作（Zaner-Bloser 和 D'Nealian 的目标）来说，并不是你没有提出要点，而是你在使用你的整个手臂。

赞纳-布洛瑟的科学主张几乎肯定是值得怀疑的，但在文字处理器出现之前，在不看自己的写作的情况下做笔记是一项关键技能，或者根据我的经验。

这是一个非常不同的世界，与古代的抄写员甚至罗马草书相比，后者只有羽毛笔，并且没有真正连接字母。

如果你研究秘书手、斜体手和宫廷手，很多都与风格和偏好有关，美国《独立宣言》是用秘书手写的，当时这在官方文件中已经流行了几个世纪。莎士比亚还写了他的戏剧《秘书汉德》，而那个时代的女士们会使用“意大利风格”斜体。

不幸的是，似乎有很多背后的解释，在没有直接证据的情况下，真正的历史就像泥巴一样清晰，或者更准确地说，没有像赞纳-布洛瑟那样的说法。

[0] https://archive.org/details/armmovementmetho00zane/page/n3/m...

children.author: ksenzee
children.textRawHtml:
To clarify my point, I am fairly sure the issue is not fountain pens requiring less pressure to write with than everything else, but rather ballpoint pens requiring more pressure than all earlier pen technology. I have not used a dip pen myself, but I can't imagine it would require pressure to write.

In other words, all of the writing tools in common use since ~1950 make it easy to separate your letters, but before the ballpoint pen became commonplace, every writer had had the experience of using a pen that makes connecting letters easier than separating them. That's the experience most of us today are missing.
children.textZhHtml:
为了澄清我的观点，我相当确定问题不是钢笔比其他笔需要更少的压力来书写，而是圆珠笔比所有早期的笔技术需要更大的压力。我自己没有用过蘸水笔，但我无法想象它会需要压力来书写。

换句话说，自 1950 年以来所有常用的书写工具都可以轻松地将字母分开，但在圆珠笔普及之前，每个作家都有过使用笔的经验，这种笔使连接字母比分开字母更容易。这是我们今天大多数人所缺少的经历。

I used ballpoint pens in school but I don't like the process: my hand often feels too tense, and getting handwriting legible is a lot of effort. Once I switched to fountain pens I enjoy the process a lot more, and the result generally look better without much effort.

I'm sure many people are OK with ballpoint pens and might even prefer the feel.

Fountain pen (+ ink and paper) doesn't really cost more than a paperlike screen protector. So it can be entirely functional. But many people also enjoy it as a hobby, collecting pens and whatnot.

children.author: ngl999
children.textRawHtml:
> I don’t see how that ties to censorship inside of China.

LLMs are parrots, when they are trained on English data they behave like English / western speakers which carries the __western__ values.

China would never want a shiny model deployed by some solemn state-own institute to pitch western values like democracy or freedom of speech.

So China is better off starting with Chinese content in the first place, but only to find out it shoots itself in the foot, because censorship __removes__ Chinese content from the Internet, and it __prevents__ truth-reflecting, i.e. quality, content from appearing.

When this is realized to be not sufficient, and they have to use English content, the English content needs to be censored, too.

So compared to other models trained on the uncensored set, the Chinese models are trained on the data sets that is likely smaller. And since high quality content is suppressed, there is likely less high quality training sets. Therefore, their models likely suck.

(Meta knows the importance of high quality training sets so that it started distilling its own employees who are smart.)

> produce GPUs that are competitive

The most recently known advanced process in China is some kind that requires multiple exposures in DUV machines. This already limits the cost to a minimum that's probably not economical.

For GPUs to be competitive, there's more to the hardware. Driver also matters. GPU drivers these days are compilers in disguise. How many high quality compiler projects have we heard of from China?

It's unlikely for both the hardware and the software of a Chinese GPU to deliver what's boasted in its marketing material.
children.textZhHtml:

comments.author: microtonal
comments.textRawHtml:
I am generally in favor of security improvements, but I do not really see much of a benefit here. This attack vector requires both that the user enabled developer settings and that they have remote adb enabled. So, this does not seem to be a realistic attack vector for 99.9% of the users and most of the other 0.1% probably know what they are doing.

The other proposed change (to restrict access to certain interfaces or IP addresses) seems good, but why not allow developers to restrict access localhost?

It reeks of trying to block Shizuku, Canta, etc. using a way that only makes it look like a side-effect.
comments.textZhHtml:
我总体上赞成改进安全性，但我并没有真正看到这里有什么好处。此攻击媒介要求用户启用开发人员设置并且启用远程 adb。因此，对于 99.9% 的用户来说，这似乎不是一个现实的攻击媒介，而其他 0.1% 的大多数用户可能知道他们在做什么。

另一个提议的更改（限制对某些接口或 IP 地址的访问）似乎不错，但为什么不允许开发人员限制访问 localhost？

它散发着试图阻止 Shizuku、Canta 等的味道，使用的方式只会使其看起来像副作用。

children.author: zaptheimpaler
children.textRawHtml:
"Security" is just a scourge on software at this point. It means 2FA on every trivial site, being logged out every few hours for no good reason, having to fuck with settings and type "disable sandbox" to run an agent in YOLO mode which still won't work over mobile, being unable to install an unsigned extension at all in firefox (not behind a setting, literally impossible - you have to get Firefox Developer Edition), sites spamming me to get passkeys which will no doubt be declared insecure and replaced by some more moronic thing when users find a way to get hacked with those too, 80 layers of access control/service identities/IAM/Oauth to host an S3 bucket, OAuth everywhere that won't even work on a headless device, banking websites that want their own special snowflake app as 2FA instead of using TOTP, banning VPNs and slowly rolling out completely real identity surveillance on every corner of the internet to "protect the children", ban open-weight models because the numbers are going to send your data to China, and it just goes on and on and on..

When is this insanity going to stop? I really think the IT security industry ought to be ashamed of itself. Security has become a totalizing value that trumps every other value - convenience, user-friendliness, privacy, hackability, openness, just anything at all in the name of MORE SECURITY.
children.textZhHtml:
“安全”在这一点上只是软件的祸害。这意味着每个微不足道的网站都会出现 2FA，每隔几个小时就会无缘无故地退出，必须搞乱设置并输入“禁用沙箱”才能在 YOLO 模式下运行代理，但在移动设备上仍然无法工作，根本无法在 Firefox 中安装未签名的扩展（不是在设置后面，实际上是不可能的 - 你必须获得 Firefox 开发版），网站向我发送垃圾邮件以获取密码，这无疑会被声明为不安全，并在用户发现时被一些更愚蠢的东西所取代一种被黑客攻击的方法，80层访问控制/服务身份/IAM/Oauth来托管S3存储桶，OAuth无处不在，甚至无法在无头设备上工作，银行网站希望自己的特殊雪花应用程序作为2FA而不是使用TOTP，禁止VPN并在互联网的每个角落慢慢推出完全真实的身份监控以“保护孩子”，禁止开放权重模型，因为这些数字会将你的数据发送到中国，以及它就这样一直持续下去……

这种疯狂什么时候才能停止？我真的认为 IT 安全行业应该为自己感到羞耻。安全性已经成为一种综合价值，超越了其他所有价值——便利性、用户友好性、隐私性、可破解性、开放性，以及任何以“更多安全”为名的东西。

children.author: AnthonyMouse
children.textRawHtml:
There is a simple and highly accurate heuristic to tell if a security measure is reasonable:

Is it an open standard that anyone can permissionlessly implement?

When the answer is yes, there is a high probability that it's something reasonable, e.g. TOTP.

When the answer is no, what you will find behind the curtain is either a fool or a crook.
children.textZhHtml:
有一个简单且高度准确的启发式方法可以判断安全措施是否合理：

它是任何人都可以无需许可实施的开放标准吗？

当答案是肯定时，很可能它是合理的，例如TOTP。

当答案是否定的时，你会发现幕后的人要么是傻子，要么是骗子。

children.author: TeMPOraL
children.textRawHtml:
This heuristic is not covering the dimensions of interest here, because it fails to address the key security questions (that the industry usually wants people to not even think about):

Who is doing the securing, whose interests are being secured, and against who/what?

Security isn't an unqualified good thing to have. It's just an instrument of control. Who wields it and how are the paramount questions. You can have an "open standard that anyone can permissionlessly implement", aimed at protecting interest of third parties, by securing the device from its actual owner. In fact, that describes many, if not most, security measures introduced in computing over the past 20 years, especially on the web and mobile devices.
children.textZhHtml:
这种启发式方法没有涵盖这里感兴趣的维度，因为它无法解决关键的安全问题（业界通常希望人们根本不去思考这些问题）：

谁在进行安全保护，谁的利益受到保护，以及针对谁/什么？

安全并不是一件绝对好的事情。它只是一个控制工具。谁运用它以及如何运用它是最重要的问题。您可以拥有一个“任何人都可以在未经许可的情况下实施的开放标准”，旨在通过保护设备免受其实际所有者的侵害来保护第三方的利益。事实上，这描述了过去 20 年计算领域引入的许多（如果不是大多数）安全措施，尤其是在网络和移动设备上。

children.author: AnthonyMouse
children.textRawHtml:
> You can have an "open standard that anyone can permissionlessly implement", aimed at protecting interest of third parties, by securing the device from its actual owner.

comments.author: projektfu
comments.textRawHtml:
Hallowell and Ratey, who write about ADHD, suggested a new entity for the current world: VAST, the variable attention stimulus trait. It is like ADHD but it is culturally induced and not presumed to be due to an innate deficiency in executive function.

"Beyond the sources of biologically based ADHD, there are a lot of people who act as if they have ADHD but on close inspection turn out not to have the diagnosable condition. These are the people who have ADHD-like symptoms caused by the conditions of modern life. Their “ADHD” is a response to the massive increase in stimuli that now bombard our brains and our world....

"Modern life has trained our brains to go faster and faster, to do more and more, to receive and transmit 24/7, and to require constant stimulation—be it from movies, TV, conversation, even news, as well as the minute-to-minute living of our lives. Most of us can go no more than a few seconds without looking for a screen."

It is likely to me that different people have different breaking points, and so one person may recognize the introduction of the smartphone or debut of TikTok as the point where they lost the ability to focus, and another may date it to the rise of LLMs.

Hallowell, E. M., & Ratey, J. J. (2021). ADHD 2.0: New science and essential strategies for thriving with distraction—from childhood through adulthood.
comments.textZhHtml:
Hallowell 和 Ratey 撰写了有关 ADHD 的文章，为当前世界提出了一个新实体：VAST，即可变注意力刺激特征。 它类似于 ADHD，但它是由文化引起的，而不是由于执行功能的先天缺陷所致。

“除了基于生物学的 ADHD 的来源之外，还有很多人表现得好像患有 ADHD，但经过仔细检查，结果发现并不具有可诊断的病症。这些人因现代生活条件而出现类似 ADHD 的症状。他们的“ADHD”是对现在轰炸我们的刺激大量增加的反应。大脑和我们的世界......

“现代生活训练我们的大脑运行得越来越快，做的事情越来越多，24/7 接收和传输，并且需要不断的刺激——无论是来自电影、电视、谈话、甚至新闻，还是我们生活中的每时每刻。我们大多数人在不寻找屏幕的情况下最多只能走几秒钟。”

对我来说，不同的人可能有不同的转折点，因此一个人可能会认为智能手机的推出或 TikTok 的首次亮相是他们失去注意力的能力，而另一个人可能会将其追溯到法学硕士的兴起。

Hallowell, E. M., & Ratey, J. J. (2021)。ADHD 2.0:从童年到成年，如何在分心的情况下茁壮成长的新科学和基本策略。

Many are built on wrong principles because the prompt authors aren't savvy and don't know better. Some authors (I've encountered this in the OpenStreetMap community) even have the gall to pretend that their code is a gift that we now have to host and maintain. Aside from these quality and community issues, build and test pipelines also take a lot of compute resources, and with large growth in projects, that will increase as well. That the author of the proposal wants to avoid this makes a ton of sense to me.

But it also drives a lot of projects away because maybe you later want to use LLM assistance (imagine LLMs got twice as good as they are today), or maybe the auto-generated tests might become >50% of the code. You'd have to migrate your repository and community away from Codeberg. Why take that risk? It's just not a worry I feel that developers need. They're looking to get away from Microsoft (GitHub) for their open source project and that's the point where Codeberg should be a no-brainer

We're an open source community and so the mass stealing of all our work to feed LLM training which heats the world and causes (at least temporarily) giant price hikes in consumer hardware... there's a lot to say for more ethical training and use of LLMs, but does it matter at all if Codeberg bans LLM output? Won't we just make ourselves obsolete? Idk. It's multifaceted and this proposal seems too vague and blunt for me. That's not an option that's set in stone btw, just my current understanding of the different aspects
children.textZhHtml:
所以我投了反对票，部分原因是我觉得文本没有公正地对待这样一个多方面的主题。

如果 Codeberg 上的所有项目都是人工编写的，那将是一个巨大的质量印记！现在有很多项目推出，有人觉得他们做了一件很酷的事情，但它在第一个边缘情况下就崩溃了，并且完全无法维护。许多内容都是建立在错误的原则之上的，因为提示作者不精明并且不了解更多。一些作者（我在 OpenStreetMap 社区中遇到过这种情况）甚至厚颜无耻地假装他们的代码是我们现在必须托管和维护的礼物。除了这些质量和社区问题之外，构建和测试管道还占用大量计算资源，并且随着项目的大幅增长，计算资源也会增加。该提案的作者希望避免这种情况对我来说很有意义。

但它也会赶走很多项目，因为也许你以后想要使用 LLM 帮助（想象一下 LLM 的质量是今天的两倍），或者自动生成的测试可能会占到代码的 50% 以上。您必须将存储库和社区从 Codeberg 迁移出去。为什么要冒这个风险？我觉得开发人员不需要担心这个问题。他们希望摆脱 Microsoft (GitHub) 的开源项目，这就是 Codeberg 应该是理所当然的事情

我们是一个开源社区，因此大量窃取我们所有的工作来提供 LLM 培训，这让世界变得热火朝天，并导致（至少暂时）消费硬件价格大幅上涨……对于更多道德培训和 LLM 的使用有很多话要说，但如果 Codeberg 禁止 LLM 输出，这有什么关系吗？我们不会让自己变得过时吗？我不知道。它是多方面的，这个提议对我来说似乎太模糊和生硬了。顺便说一句，这不是一个一成不变的选择，只是我目前对不同方面的理解

children.author: microtonal
children.textRawHtml:
You'd have to migrate your repository and community away from Codeberg. Why take that risk? It's just not a worry I feel that developers need.

I feel like we are already there. I am not vibecoding a lot, but I certainly use LLM-assisted coding now for most of my work. Once you go beyond vibe coding, an LLM feels a lot like a compiler from your well-specified ideas to code. So, to some extend, these restrictions feel like disallowing a higher-level programming language in a time when everyone was still writing machine code.

I understand where this decision is coming from (especially because they have been under attack by LLM bots) and it is well within their right, but the vague language adds a lot of uncertainty:

You must not share projects that mostly consist of code written by "generative AI"-tools

It's clear that this excludes vibe coding. But what about LLM-assisted coding, where the developer writes very clear instructions of what to do and carefully reviews every line? In such cases a project 'mostly consist of code written by "generative AI"-tools', but the quality is probably not worse than fully hand-written code, especially because an LLM is often more able to 'think' of all kinds of corner cases.

I have some projects on Codeberg and donate monthly, but I have to reconsider both, since with this change Codeberg does not really align with how I work anymore. The projects that I have on Codeberg are largely human-written, but certainly use LLM-assistance for new code.

At any rate, I guess I'm back to GitHub until I have found a better alternative.
children.textZhHtml:
您必须将存储库和社区从 Codeberg 迁移出去。为什么要冒这个风险？我觉得开发人员不需要担心这个问题。

我觉得我们已经在那里了。我不经常编码，但我现在的大部分工作肯定都使用法学硕士辅助编码。一旦你超越了氛围编码，法学硕士感觉很像一个编译器，可以将你明确的想法转化为代码。因此，在某种程度上，这些限制感觉就像在每个人仍在编写机器代码的时代不允许使用更高级的编程语言。

我理解这个决定的来源（特别是因为他们受到了LLM机器人的攻击）并且这完全在他们的权利范围内，但是模糊的语言增加了很多不确定性：

您不得共享主要由“生成式人工智能”工具编写的代码组成的项目

很明显，这不包括振动编码。但是，LLM 辅助编码又如何呢？开发人员会编写非常清晰的说明并仔细检查每一行？在这种情况下，项目“主要由“生成式人工智能”工具编写的代码组成”，但质量可能并不比完全手写的代码差，特别是因为法学硕士通常更能够“思考”各种极端情况。

我在 Codeberg 上有一些项目，并且每月都会捐赠，但我必须重新考虑这两个项目，因为经过此更改，Codeberg 不再与我的工作方式真正保持一致。我在 Codeberg 上的项目大部分是人工编写的，但肯定会使用 LLM 协助来编写新代码。

无论如何，我想我会回到 GitHub，直到找到更好的替代方案。

children.author: therealpygon
children.textRawHtml:
A big seal of quality because it is human written? Maybe in narrow spaces but in general, I’d put money on the average developer being significantly worse at writing code with bugs than an AI. It’s codebergs infra so their choice, but it seems like an overly simplistic solution to a complicated advancing technology, in that it is a threadbare line between “vibe-coded” and “complex agent harness with human oversight and review”.

Also, I’m actually quite happy with some of the vibe-coded apps I use. Handy is an example, which started as a vibecoded app, and is fantastic for STT/dictation. It seems like a literal baby with the bath water approach.
children.textZhHtml:
因为是人写的，所以质量大印章？也许在狭窄的空间里，但总的来说，我认为普通开发人员在编写带有错误的代码方面比人工智能差得多。这是他们的选择，但对于复杂的先进技术来说，这似乎是一个过于简单的解决方案，因为它是“振动编码”和“具有人工监督和审查的复杂代理工具”之间的一条陈旧界限。

另外，我实际上对我使用的一些振动编码应用程序非常满意。 Handy 就是一个例子，它最初是一个 vivicoded 应用程序，非常适合 STT/听写。这看起来就像是一个字面意思上的婴儿洗澡水方法。

children.author: lelanthran
children.textRawHtml:
> I’d put money on the average developer being significantly worse at writing code with bugs than an AI.

I'd put money on the average AI-coded project being of a worse quality, simply because the number of vibe-coders with no experience now outnumbers actual coders using AI-assist around 10 to 1.

I'm literally seeing companies being pitched with B2B products written by people who had never written a program before, even as a hobby!

AI on average might write better code, but there's no way AI prompted by a shoe salesman is going to be better than code written by a person with even 2x years of experience.
children.textZhHtml:
> 我认为普通开发人员在编写带有错误的代码方面比人工智能差得多。

我认为平均人工智能编码项目的质量较差，仅仅是因为现在没有经验的振动编码器的数量与使用人工智能辅助的实际编码器的数量大约为 10 比 1。

我确实看到公司正在推销由从未编写过程序的人编写的 B2B 产品以前，即使只是作为一种爱好！

平均而言，人工智能可能会编写出更好的代码，但由鞋推销员推动的人工智能不可能比由拥有两年经验的人编写的代码更好。

children.author: therealpygon
children.textRawHtml:
Definitely agree, though not sure I agree on the why (I’ve also disagreed with the conclusions of similar studies as well).

Programming is high-function job that requires knowledge in a million areas. I know I certainly can’t keep all of them in my head and frequently had to go back to documentation, or look up parameters, or how to implement that one pattern I used that one time that worked well in this situation or… The conclusion they draw is basically that “programming also made me dumber” because I didn’t remember them after working on a completely different project in a different language. I wholeheartedly agree thinking skills can atrophy with AI, but my view is that they are likely replaced by different thinking skills in other areas (e.g. improved prompting, improved structure, understanding harnesses, and so on. I used to write batch scripts often; I stopped, now I suck at it. If I paid someone else to write a batch script, I won’t suddenly remember everything I’ve forgotten but plenty people condemn AI for the equivalent result of paying someone else to do the programming.
children.textZhHtml:

编程是一项高功能工作，需要一百万个领域的知识。我知道我当然不能把它们全部记在脑子里，经常不得不返回文档，或者查找参数，或者如何实现我曾经使用过的一种模式，在这种情况下效果很好，或者……他们得出的结论基本上是“编程也让我变得更笨”，因为在用不同的语言完成了一个完全不同的项目后，我不记得它们了。我完全同意人工智能会削弱思维技能，但我的观点是，它们很可能会被其他领域的不同思维技能所取代（例如改进的提示、改进的结构、理解工具等等。我以前经常编写批处理脚本；我停止了，现在我很糟糕。如果我付钱给别人写批处理脚本，我不会突然记住我忘记的一切，但很多人谴责人工智能与付钱给别人做编程的结果相同。

children.author: onion2k
children.textRawHtml:
I’d put money on the average developer being significantly worse at writing code with bugs than an AI.

I'd take that bet if it was measured in "bugs per day" instead of "bugs per LOC". LLMs generate far fewer bugs in absolute terms, but they also generate far more code, so it probably balances out if everything is equal. I think LLMs will actually lead to more bugs just because they're usually working with poorly defined requirements (prompts) and they guess to fill in the gaps based on the averages of their training data. A lot of those guesses are wrong.

Where LLMs win though is the severity. An LLM will write buggy code in the sense that it doesn't do what you wanted it, but not so much in the sense of security or data loss bugs. They get that right more than humans because they're trained to care about that stuff. There's far more "how to write good code" content in the training data than "how to not care about security and go fast" content (because writing that would be weird!)
children.textZhHtml:
我认为普通开发人员在编写带有错误的代码方面比人工智能差得多。

如果以“每天的错误数”而不是“每个 LOC 的错误数”来衡量，我会接受这个赌注。从绝对意义上讲，法学硕士产生的错误要少得多，但它们也会产生更多的代码，因此如果一切都相同，它可能会平衡。我认为法学硕士实际上会导致更多错误，因为他们通常会处理定义不明确的需求（提示），并且他们根据训练数据的平均值猜测填补空白。其中很多猜测都是错误的。

法学硕士获胜的关键在于其严重程度。法学硕士会编写有错误的代码，因为它没有按照您想要的方式执行，但在安全或数据丢失错误方面则不然。他们比人类更能做到这一点，因为他们受过训练来关心这些事情。训练数据中“如何编写好的代码”内容远多于“如何不关心安全性并快速运行”内容（因为这样写会很奇怪！）

comments.author: novaleaf
comments.textRawHtml:
Some irony: I subscribe to Claude and Codex (20x plans), and now Kimi.

Why Kimi? because K3 is the only frontier model I can have a serious conversation with about my product's security.

(I did apply for OpenAi's Cyber Pilot but got no response)
comments.textZhHtml:
有些讽刺：我订阅了 Claude 和 Codex（20x 计划），现在订阅了 Kimi。

为什么选择 Kimi？ 因为K3是唯一一个我可以认真讨论我的产品安全性的前沿模型。

（我确实申请了OpenAi的Cyber Pilot，但没有得到回复）

children.author: Agingcoder
children.textRawHtml:
Yeah I tried to have a conversation about security yesterday with Claude and it immediately stopped me - I was taken aback, I didn’t expect it at all.

This is highly problematic.
children.textZhHtml:
是的，昨天我试图与 Claude 讨论安全问题，但它立即阻止了我 - 我大吃一惊，我根本没想到会这样。

这是一个很大的问题。

children.author: gck1
children.textRawHtml: Claude's "I'm going to draw the line here", "This is where I'm going to hold the ground" always rubs me the wrong way. Classifiers rejecting a request are one thing, but there's something very troubling about machine saying "I'm going to draw the line".
children.textZhHtml: 克劳德的“我要在这里划清界限”、“这是我要坚守阵地的地方”总是让我感到不舒服。分类器拒绝请求是一回事，但机器说“我要划清界限”是非常令人不安的。

children.author: whycome
children.textRawHtml: Lol that’s so hostile. It’s insane how much the language of these models create real unaddressed human reactions.
children.textZhHtml: 哈哈，这太有敌意了。这些模型的语言在多大程度上创造了真实的、未解决的人类反应，这真是太疯狂了。

children.textZhHtml:
最近克劳德帮助我解决了一个安全问题，当它存在时，克劳德会说话。

children.author: sigmoid10
children.textRawHtml: I found GPT 5.3 was the last model that was sufficiently competent and still open to discuss security on my own github repos. 5.4 started refusing to even look at potential problems, albeit not consistently. I'm considering a Kimi subscription, but I know many employers will simply not be on board with this and I don't know if I get enough personal use out of this for the few things I run on servers. When those companies realize what they're currently missing out on, it will be a game-changer.
children.textZhHtml: 我发现 GPT 5.3 是最后一个足够强大的模型，并且仍然可以在我自己的 github 存储库上讨论安全性。 5.4 甚至开始拒绝查看潜在的问题，尽管并非始终如一。我正在考虑订阅 Kimi，但我知道许多雇主根本不会同意这一点，而且我不知道我是否能从中获得足够的个人用途来用于我在服务器上运行的一些东西。当这些公司意识到他们目前错过了什么时，游戏规则将会改变。

I could never have gotten there through Codex alone.

children.author: rmast
children.textRawHtml: Was it applying to the program for an organization or individual? The description for the individual application page makes it sound pretty straightforward compared to getting access for an organization.

children.author: novaleaf
children.textRawHtml:
I applied for individuals. I did their verification steps and answered questions in a few minutes, so that was indeed easy. The problem is that was all that happened. No followup, no access, no denial. When I tried to reapply it tells me I can't apply again.

OpenAi (and Anthropic) have no incentive to allow security access to individuals. I'm not a deep-pocket org or influential gov agency. Allowing individuals increases the risk of bad press (what if I do something naughty and talk about it?) so best to ignore us.
children.textZhHtml:
我申请的是个人。 我在几分钟内完成了他们的验证步骤并回答了问题，所以这确实很容易。 问题是这就是发生的一切。 没有后续，没有访问，没有拒绝。当我尝试重新申请时，它告诉我无法再次申请。

OpenAi（和 Anthropic）没有动力允许个人进行安全访问。 我不是财力雄厚的组织或有影响力的政府机构。 允许个人会增加负面新闻的风险（如果我做了一些顽皮的事情并谈论它怎么办？）所以最好忽略我们。

children.author: nicce
children.textRawHtml: I think individual one still has less capabilities than the one they offer for organizations.
children.textZhHtml: 我认为个人的能力仍然不如他们为组织提供的能力。

children.author: torginus
children.textRawHtml:
The product strategy of 'consumer-grade' AI making deliberately insecure software, and then selling you limited access to the model that can fix it (if they think you deserve to pay them) is just diabolical.

(Grade 3 AI which can hack both previous tiers is exclusively sold to the highest bidder.)
children.textZhHtml:
“消费者级”人工智能的产品策略是故意制造不安全的软件，然后向您出售可以修复该问题的模型的有限访问权限（如果他们认为您值得向他们付费），这简直就是恶魔般的行为。

（可以破解前两层的 3 级人工智能将独家出售给出价最高者。）

children.author: novaleaf
children.textRawHtml: I don't think it's nefarious, but the end result leads to a pretty frustrating experience by anybody needing actual security work. (and without the organizational deep pockets to obtain SOC 2 attestation)
children.textZhHtml: 我不认为这是邪恶的，但最终结果会给任何需要实际安全工作的人带来相当令人沮丧的体验。 （并且没有组织雄厚的财力来获得 SOC 2 认证）

comments.author: dhx
comments.textRawHtml:
AWS's 3 data centres in me-south-1 are:

BAH53 (Manama): https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/1492345589

  An adjoining substation to BAH53 had one of it's two main buildings damaged/destroyed about 2026-07-16 per https://soaratlas.com/maps/asia-damage-to-data-center-power-substation-bahrain-jul-16th-2026-142024

  Then about 2026-07-22 BAH53 itself was damaged/destroyed per https://soaratlas.com/maps/asia-damage-to-amazon-web-services-bahrain-jul-22nd-2026-142112

  Possibly the least defended of the three sites as there is no air/missile defence battery in between this site and Iran.
BAH54 (Zallaq): https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/1359931661

  No media reports about this data centre being attacked previously. Possibly the safest of the three as there are at least two (probably three) air/missile defence batteries in between this site and Iran.
BAH55 (Hamala): https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/956069872

  Apparently the Batelco DC.1 data centre adjoining (and apparently critical to) BAH55 was damaged/destroyed about 2026-04-01 per https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cgk28nj0lrjo _or_ the adjoining substation to these two facilities was damaged/destroyed -- news articles are hard to follow as to what exactly might have been damaged and the extent of damage caused.

  Middle ground for defence with one or two (maybe three) air/missile defence batteries between this site and Iran, depending on where drones/missiles are launched from.
If these data centres are rebuilt, you'd maybe expect them to be rebuilt in new locations behind existing _permanent_ (and seemingly quite expensive) air/missile defence batteries in Bahrain (https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/1492281507 and https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/1492953902). Based on the permanency of those air/missile defence batteries it doesn't look like the government of Bahrain are expecting things to get safer for data centre hosting in Bahrain any time soon.

children.author: Someone
children.textRawHtml:
> It probably wouldn't help much against ballistic missiles, but it might make it more resilient against drone attacks.

I think the two kinds of attacks are so different that they require different defenses.

Drones need not fly in straight lines. Data centers need ventilation, providing a path for drones. Putting grids in a ventilation shaft will stop the first drone, but a coordinated attack will use one drone to blow up defenses and a second/third/etc one to reach the target
children.textZhHtml:
> 它可能对对抗弹道导弹没有多大帮助，但它可能会使其对无人机攻击更有弹性。

我认为这两种攻击非常不同，因此需要不同的防御。

无人机不需要直线飞行。数据中心需要通风，为无人机提供通道。将网格放入通风井将阻止第一架无人机，但协调攻击将使用一架无人机炸毁防御，然后使用第二架/第三架/等等无人机到达目标

简单地为数据和计算提供全局冗余可能比将数据中心放入地堡要便宜得多。

children.textRawHtml: Not all businesses want to pay the premium for that level of redundancy. Businesses with lower margins want resilient service at a lower price point. With AI and contributed shift to cloud, the demand for lowering TCO for a greater share of the larger pie becomes greater.
children.textZhHtml: 并非所有企业都愿意为这种程度的冗余支付额外费用。利润率较低的企业希望以较低的价格获得弹性服务。随着人工智能和向云计算的转变，降低总体拥有成本以获取更大份额的需求变得更大。

children.author: londons_explore
